'''Cody Allen Zeller''' (born October 5, 1992) is a sophomore [[basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball]] team at [[Indiana University Bloomington|Indiana University]]. Zeller is considered one of the top players in college basketball, known in particular for a "high basketball IQ" and unselfish play.<ref name="Givony">{{cite web|last=Givony|first=Jonathan|title=NBA Draft Prospect of the Week: Cody Zeller|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Cody-Zeller-6241/|publisher=DraftExpress|date=8 December 2011}}</ref><ref name="ESPN"/>

==Personal==
Zeller is from [[Washington, Indiana]] and the nephew of former NBA player [[Al Eberhard]]. He is the youngest brother of former [[North Carolina Tar Heels|North Carolina]] and current [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] center [[Tyler Zeller]] and former [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish|Notre Dame]] and former [[Phoenix Suns]] forward-center [[Luke Zeller]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Player Bio: Cody Zeller|url=http://iuhoosiers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/zeller_cody00.html}}</ref> Despite pressures brought on by unusually high expectations, commentators have noted his humility and work ethic, along with "dry wit and prankster's mirth." <ref name="ESPN">{{cite news|last=O'Neil|first=Dana|title=Cody Zeller sparks Hoosiers' turnaround|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7442851/unassuming-cody-zeller-keys-indiana-hoosiers-turnaround-college-basketball|accessdate=7 April 2012|newspaper=ESPN|date=11 January 2012}}</ref>

==High school==
In [[his]] freshman year of high school, Zeller averaged 2.5 points and 1.4 rebounds per game as his team, the [[Washington High School (Washington, Indiana)|Washington Hatchets]], won a Class 3A [[Indiana High School Athletic Association|IHSAA]] state championship. During his sophomore season, he averaged 15.0 points and 6.8 rebounds. In his junior year Zeller led Washington to a Class 3A state championship, averaging 20.5 points and 11.4 rebounds per game. Following that season he was named an Indiana Junior All-Star. In his senior year of high school, Zeller averaged 24.6 points per game, 13.1 rebounds per game and 3.3 assists per game while leading the Hatchets to the Class 3A [[Indiana High School Athletic Association|IHSAA]] state championship, the third title of his career. Zeller led the Indiana Senior All-Stars to a two-game sweep of the Kentucky All-Stars. He played [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball for the Indiana Elite program and led the USA 2011 squad to the Adidas Nations Championship in Chicago during the summer of 2010.

Following the end of his senior season, Zeller was named [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]], the state's highest honor for high school players and an award both of his elder brothers also won. Zeller became the 26th Mr. Basketball from the state of Indiana to play for the Hoosiers. He was a 2011 [[McDonald's All American]] player and scored 10 points, pulled down three rebounds and had three assists in the nationally acclaimed all-star game. Other honors Zeller won in his high school career include first team All-State honors from the Indiana Basketball Coaches Association, the [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] accolades in Indiana, and a [[Parade All-American]]. According to [[ESPN]] Zeller was the 13th best overall recruit in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cody Zeller 2011 Basketball Recruiting Profile|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/56338/cody-zeller}}</ref> Scout.com had him rated 12th nationally and third at his position, while [[Rivals.com]] had him slotted 15th in the country and fourth at his position.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cody Zeller- Yahoo! Sports|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Cody-Zeller-86160;_ylt=Asn8Gd8NYtT3v5roiZKKes_VO5B4}}</ref>

==College career==
On November 12, 2010, Zeller committed to play for [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana University]], turning down offers from [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] and [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Eisenberg|first=Jeff|title=Cody Zeller's commitment means Indiana's on its way back|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/blog/the_dagger/post/Cody-Zeller-s-commitment-means-Indiana-s-on-its-?urn=ncaab-284660|accessdate=3 April 2012|newspaper=Yahoo|date=12 November 2010}}</ref> Upon his commitment he was labeled "the savior of Indiana basketball."<ref name="ESPN"/> At the time Coach [[Tom Crean (basketball)|Tom Crean]] noted, "He's the most mentally focused kid I've ever recruited ... I see a young man that has mental toughness that is not normal."<ref name="Corazza">{{cite news|last=Corazza|first=Ryan|title=That's a Wrap: Cody Zeller|url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2012/04/09/thats-a-wrap-cody-zeller/|accessdate=9 April 2012|newspaper=Inside the Hall|date=9 April 2012}}</ref>

===Freshman season===
In Zeller's first year as a Hoosier during the [[2011–12 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2011-12 season]] he led the team with 15.6 points and 6.6 rebounds per game, while shooting 62.3 percent (200-of-321) from the field and 75.5 percent (163-of-216) from the free throw line.<ref name="Corazza"/> He ranked fourth in the country in field goal percentage, led the [[Big Ten Conference]] and posted the second highest percentage in school history.<ref name="IUPressRelease">{{cite news|title=Watford, Zeller Will Be Back For Indiana Men's Basketball|url=http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041012aab.html|accessdate=10 April 2012|newspaper=Indiana Univ Athletic Dept|date=10 April 2012}}</ref> His offensive rating of 126.8 ranked him 14th nationwide. Zeller was the Big Ten's Freshman of the Year, as voted on by the coaches, after earning Big Ten Freshman of the Week seven times.<ref>{{cite web|title=Zeller named Big Ten Freshman of the Year|url=http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030512aaf.html}}</ref> He was also Second Team All-Big Ten and a First Team Freshman All-American. He was a finalist for the Wayman Tisdale Award (USBWA National Freshman of the Year) and was a candidate for the John Wooden Award and Oscar Robertson Trophy.<ref name="IUPressRelease"/>

With the addition of Zeller to the team, the Hoosiers' record in [[2011–12 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2011-2012]] improved by fifteen games over the prior season, making it the largest single turnaround in the NCAA that year. The Hoosiers earned a number four seed in the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA Tournament]] and defeated [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]] in the second round. After defeating [[Virginia Commonwealth University Rams men's basketball|VCU]] in the third round, the Hoosiers lost in the Sweet Sixteen to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], the eventual national champions.

===Sophomore Season===
Although projected to be a top ten pick in the [[2012 NBA Draft]], Zeller decided to return for his sophomore season at Indiana, along with teammate [[Christian Watford]]. In a statement issued by the Indiana Athletic Department, he said, "I grew up hoping that one day I would get the opportunity to play in the NBA, but at this point I'm not ready for my college experience to be over...My college experience at IU this year has exceeded my expectations, on and off the court. I look forward to playing at Assembly Hall next year in front of the greatest fans in the country."<ref name="IUPressRelease"/> 

Due in part to Zeller's leadership, the Indiana Hoosiers finished the [[2012–13 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2012-13 season]] as the outright Big Ten champions. He finished the regular season as the conference's third highest scorer (16.8 points) and second highest rebounder (8.2), along with second in the league in shooting at 57% while only trailing teammate Victor Oladipo in the Big Ten.<ref name="2013awards">{{cite web | url=http://indiana.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=1482278 | title=Oladipo, Zeller head IU Big 10 honorees | publisher=Rivals.com | accessdate=March 12, 2013 | author=Rabjohns, Jeff}}</ref>

Zeller accumulated numerous post-season awards. He was named a [[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2013 All-American]] by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] (2nd Team) and ''[[Sporting News]]'' (3rd Team). He was also named First Team All-Big Ten by both the coaches and media, as well as a First Team Academic All-American.[12]   Fans voted him The 2013 Premier Player of College Basketball.

==Professional career==
At the end of his sophomore season, Zeller decided to enter the [[2013 NBA Draft]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/id/9155252/indiana-hoosiers-cody-zeller-leaving-nba-draft-report-says|accessdate=10 April 2013}}</ref> along with teammate [[Victor Oladipo]]. He is projected to still be a Top 10 pick, if not a late lottery pick.

==Player profile==
Analysts describe Zeller as having "the outstanding combination of mobility, scoring instincts and aggressiveness," while also being "an incredibly agile and fluid big man who runs the floor well and has the explosiveness to play above the rim on a regular basis."<ref name="Givony"/> Zeller is also known for a "high basketball IQ" and unselfish play.<ref name="ESPN"/> Other commentators have noted his "high motor" and that he is "the best screen-and-roll frontcourt player in college basketball....He sprints to the screen, reads slips and has great hands. He is hard to keep off the glass and has the versatility to play in the high post as well as on the baseline."<ref>{{cite web | url=http://insider.espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/blog/_/name/ncbexperts/id/8916720/michigan-trey-burke-top-10-closers-country-college-basketball | title=Top 10 closers in college hoops | publisher=ESPN.com | date=February 5, 2013 | accessdate=February 5, 2013 | author=Greenberg, Seth}}</ref>
